Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: 1583 – 17 December 1663) was a southwest African paramount ruler who ruled as queen of the Ambundu Kingdoms of Ndongo (1624–1663) and Matamba (1631–1663), in present-day northern Angola.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Nzinga received military and political training as a child, and she demonstrated an aptitude for defusing political crises as an ambassador to the Portuguese Empire. Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The Portuguese declared war on Ndongo in 1626 and by 1628, Njinga's army had been severely depleted and they went into exile.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In search of allies, she married _____ warlord Kasanje
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In search of allies, she married Imbangala warlord Kasanje.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Using this new alliance to rebuild her forces, she conquered the Kingdom of Matamba from _____ to 1635
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Using this new alliance to rebuild her forces, she conquered the Kingdom of Matamba from 1631 to 1635.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In _____, she entered into an alliance with the Dutch West India Company who had captured Luanda from the Portuguese
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In 1641, she entered into an alliance with the Dutch West India Company who had captured Luanda from the Portuguese. Between 1641 and 1644, Njinga was able to reclaim large parts of Ndongo.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Between _____ and 1644, Njinga was able to reclaim large parts of Ndongo
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In 1641, she entered into an alliance with the Dutch West India Company who had captured Luanda from the Portuguese. Between 1641 and 1644, Njinga was able to reclaim large parts of Ndongo.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Alongside the Dutch, she defeated the _____ in a number of battles but was unable to take the Fortress of Massangano
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In 1641, she entered into an alliance with the Dutch West India Company who had captured Luanda from the Portuguese. Alongside the Dutch, she defeated the Portuguese in a number of battles but was unable to take the Fortress of Massangano.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In _____, the Portuguese recaptured Luanda, with the Dutch leaving Angola
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In 1648, the Portuguese recaptured Luanda, with the Dutch leaving Angola.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Njinga continued to fight the Portuguese until a peace treaty was signed in _____
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Njinga continued to fight the Portuguese until a peace treaty was signed in 1656.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In the centuries since her death, _____ has been increasingly recognized as a major historical figure in Angola and in the wider Atlantic Creole culture
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Njinga continued to fight the Portuguese until a peace treaty was signed in 1656. In the centuries since her death, Njinga has been increasingly recognized as a major historical figure in Angola and in the wider Atlantic Creole culture.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She was the daughter of Ngola (a noble title translatable to King) _____ of Ndongo
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She was the daughter of Ngola (a noble title translatable to King) Kilombo of Ndongo.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Her mother, _____ ka Nkombe, was one of her father's slave wives and his favorite concubine
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Her mother, Kengela ka Nkombe, was one of her father's slave wives and his favorite concubine. According to legend, the birthing process was very difficult for Kengela, her mother; Njinga received her name because the umbilical cord was wrapped around her neck (the Kimbundu verb kujinga means to twist or turn).

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Njinga had two sisters, Kambu, or _____ and Funji, or Lady Grace
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Njinga had two sisters, Kambu, or Lady Barbara and Funji, or Lady Grace.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She also had a brother, _____, who was heir apparent to throne
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She also had a brother, Mbandi, who was heir apparent to throne.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: As a child, _____ was greatly favored by her father
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Njinga had two sisters, Kambu, or Lady Barbara and Funji, or Lady Grace. As a child, Njinga was greatly favored by her father.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She received military training and was trained as a warrior to fight alongside her father, displaying considerable aptitude with a battle axe, the traditional weapon of _____ warriors
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She received military training and was trained as a warrior to fight alongside her father, displaying considerable aptitude with a battle axe, the traditional weapon of Ndongan warriors.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Furthermore, _____ was taught by visiting Portuguese missionaries to read and write in Portuguese
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Furthermore, Njinga was taught by visiting Portuguese missionaries to read and write in Portuguese. Common spellings found in Portuguese and English sources include Nzinga, Nzingha, Njinga, and Njingha.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Common spellings found in _____ and English sources include Nzinga, Nzingha, Njinga, and Njingha
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Furthermore, Njinga was taught by visiting Portuguese missionaries to read and write in Portuguese. Common spellings found in Portuguese and English sources include Nzinga, Nzingha, Njinga, and Njingha.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In colonial documentation, including her own manuscripts, her name was also spelled Jinga, Ginga, Zinga, _____, Zhinga, and Singa
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In colonial documentation, including her own manuscripts, her name was also spelled Jinga, Ginga, Zinga, Zingua, Zhinga, and Singa.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She was also known by her _____ name, Ana de Sousa
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She was also known by her Christian name, Ana de Sousa.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: This name—Anna de _____—was given to her when she was baptized
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: This name—Anna de Souza Nzingha—was given to her when she was baptized.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She was named Anna after the _____ woman who acted as her Godmother at the ceremony
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She was named Anna after the Portuguese woman who acted as her Godmother at the ceremony.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She helped influence who _____ was in the future
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: This name—Anna de Souza Nzingha—was given to her when she was baptized. She helped influence who Nzingha was in the future.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Her Christian surname, de Souza, came from the acting governor of Angola, João _____ de Souza
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Her Christian surname, de Souza, came from the acting governor of Angola, João Correia de Souza.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: As a monarch of Ndongo and Matamba, her native name was _____
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: As a monarch of Ndongo and Matamba, her native name was Ngola Njinga.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Ngola was the Ndongo name for the ruler and the etymological root of "_____"
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Her Christian surname, de Souza, came from the acting governor of Angola, João Correia de Souza. Ngola was the Ndongo name for the ruler and the etymological root of "Angola".

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In Portuguese, she was known as _____/Zinga/Ginga (Queen Nzinga)
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In Portuguese, she was called Rainha Nzinga/Zinga/Ginga (Queen Nzinga).

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: According to the current _____ orthography, her name is spelled Njinga Mbandi (the "j" is a voiced postalveolar fricative or "soft j" as in Portuguese and French, while the adjacent "n" is silent)
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: According to the current Kimbundu orthography, her name is spelled Njinga Mbandi (the "j" is a voiced postalveolar fricative or "soft j" as in Portuguese and French, while the adjacent "n" is silent).

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: The statue of Njinga now standing in the square of Kinaxixi in Luanda calls her "_____"
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The statue of Njinga now standing in the square of Kinaxixi in Luanda calls her "Mwene Njinga Mbande".

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: The Portuguese had first come to Ndongo in _____ when they established a trading post in Luanda with the help of the Kingdom of Kongo, Ndongo's northern rival
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The Portuguese had first come to Ndongo in 1575 when they set up a trading post in Luanda with the help of the Kingdom of Kongo, Ndongo's northern rival.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Despite several years of initial peace between Ndongo and _____, relations soured between the two kingdoms and devolved into decades of war between them
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Despite several years of initial peace between Ndongo and Portugal, relations soured between the two kingdoms and devolved into decades of war between them. Ndongo faced intense military pressure from Portugal and Kongo, both of which seized Ndongan territory.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Ndongo faced intense military pressure from _____ and Kongo, both of which seized Ndongan territory
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Despite several years of initial peace between Ndongo and Portugal, relations soured between the two kingdoms and devolved into decades of war between them. Ndongo faced intense military pressure from Portugal and Kongo, both of which seized Ndongan territory.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: By the 1580s, large parts of Ndongo had fallen under _____ control
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The Portuguese had first come to Ndongo in 1575 when they set up a trading post in Luanda with the help of the Kingdom of Kongo, Ndongo's northern rival. By the 1580s, large parts of Ndongo had fallen under Portuguese control.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In addition to territorial conquests, the _____ seized large numbers of slaves during the conflict (50,000 according to one source) and built forts inside Ndongan territory to control the slave trade
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: By the 1580s, large parts of Ndongo had fallen under Portuguese control. The Portuguese waged war in a brutal style, burning villages and taking hostages.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Ndongo rallied against the Portuguese, defeating Portugal at the Battle of Lucala in _____, but not before the kingdom had lost much of its territory
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Ndongo rallied against the Portuguese, defeating Portugal at the Battle of Lucala in 1590, but not before the kingdom had lost much of its territory.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: The conflict eroded the power of the king, with many _____ noblemen, sobas, refusing to pay tribute to the crown and some siding with the Portuguese
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: In addition to territorial conquests, the Portuguese seized large numbers of slaves during the conflict (50,000 according to one source) and built forts inside Ndongan territory to control the slave trade. The conflict eroded the power of the king, with many Ndongan noblemen, sobas, refusing to pay tribute to the crown and some siding with the Portuguese.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: By the time that Nzinga's father became king in _____, the region had been devastated by war and the power of the king greatly diminished
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: By the time that Nzinga's father became king in 1593, the region had been devastated by war and the power of the king greatly diminished.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: The situation grew worse for Ndongo when in _____ the kingdom was invaded by the Imbangala, tribal bands of warriors known for their ferocity in battle and religious fervor
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The situation grew worse for Ndongo when in 1607 the kingdom was invaded by the Imbangala, tribal bands of warriors known for their ferocity in battle and religious fervor.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: The Imbangala divided themselves into warbands, occupying _____ territory and capturing slaves
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The Imbangala divided themselves into warbands, occupying Ndongan territory and capturing slaves. The Portuguese hired some of the Imbangalans as mercenaries, and the new threat forced the Ndongan king to give up any attempts to reconquer his lost territory.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: The Portuguese hired some of the _____ as mercenaries, and the new threat forced the Ndongan king to give up any attempts to reconquer his lost territory
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The Portuguese hired some of the Imbangalans as mercenaries, and the new threat forced the Ndongan king to give up any attempts to reconquer his lost territory.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Perhaps fearing for her life, Nzinga fled to the _____ of Matamba
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Perhaps fearing for her life, Nzinga fled to the Kingdom of Matamba.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Having consolidated his power, Mbandi vowed to continue the war against the _____
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Having consolidated his power, Mbandi vowed to continue the war against the Portuguese. However, he lacked military skill, and while he was able to form an alliance with the Imbangala, the Portuguese made significant military gains.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She was the best fit for the job, as she was both of royal lineage and spoke fluent _____
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Having consolidated his power, Mbandi vowed to continue the war against the Portuguese. However, he lacked military skill, and while he was able to form an alliance with the Imbangala, the Portuguese made significant military gains.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: However, he lacked military skill, and while he was able to form an alliance with the _____, the Portuguese made significant military gains
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: However, he lacked military skill, and while he was able to form an alliance with the Imbangala, the Portuguese made significant military gains.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Faced with the Portuguese threat, in _____ he contacted Nzinga, asking her to be his emissary to the Portuguese in Luanda
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Faced with the Portuguese threat, in 1621 he contacted Nzinga, asking her to be his emissary to the Portuguese in Luanda.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Nzinga departed the _____ capital with a large retinue and was received with considerable interest in Luanda, compelling the Portuguese governor to pay for all of her party's expenses
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Nzinga departed the Ndongan capital with a large retinue and was received with considerable interest in Luanda, compelling the Portuguese governor to pay for all of her party's expenses. While Ndongo leaders typically met the Portuguese in European clothing, she chose to wear opulent traditional clothing (including feathers and jewels) of the Ndongan people, to display that their culture was not inferior.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: According to a popular story, when Nzinga arrived to meet with the _____, there were chairs for the Portuguese officials but only a mat provided for her
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She agreed to lead the diplomatic mission with the stipulation that she be granted the authority to negotiate in the king's name and permission to be baptized – an important diplomatic tool she hoped to use against the Portuguese. Nzinga departed the Ndongan capital with a large retinue and was received with considerable interest in Luanda, compelling the Portuguese governor to pay for all of her party's expenses.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: As ambassador, Nzinga's main goal was to secure peace between her people and the _____
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: According to a popular story, when Nzinga arrived to meet with the Portuguese, there were chairs for the Portuguese officials but only a mat provided for her. This type of behavior from the Portuguese was common; it was their way of displaying a "subordinate status, a status reserved for conquered Africans." In response to this, Nzinga's attendant formed herself to be her chair while she spoke to the governor face to face.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: When the _____ questioned her commitment to peace, Nzinga offered to be publicly baptized, which she was with great aplomb in Luanda
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: To this end, she promised the Portuguese an end to hostilities (describing her brother's previous actions as the mistakes of a young king), allowed Portuguese slave traders inside Ndongo, and offered to return escaped Portuguese slaves fighting in her brother's army. When the Portuguese questioned her commitment to peace, Nzinga offered to be publicly baptized, which she was with great aplomb in Luanda.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She adopted the name _____ de Sousa in honor of her godparents, Ana da Silva (the governor's wife and her ordained godmother) and Governor Joao Correia de Sousa
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She adopted the name Dona Anna de Sousa in honor of her godparents, Ana da Silva (the governor's wife and her ordained godmother) and Governor Joao Correia de Sousa.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: A peace treaty was subsequently agreed upon, and Nzinga returned to Kabasa in triumph in late _____
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: A peace treaty was subsequently agreed upon, and Nzinga returned to Kabasa in triumph in late 1622.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Despite her success in the negotiations with the _____, the peace between Ndongo and the Imbangala – themselves engaged in expanding their territory – collapsed
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: When the Portuguese questioned her commitment to peace, Nzinga offered to be publicly baptized, which she was with great aplomb in Luanda. Despite her success in the negotiations with the Portuguese, the peace between Ndongo and the Imbangala – themselves engaged in expanding their territory – collapsed.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: After a series of defeats, the _____ royal family was driven out of their court in Kabasa, putting the king in exile and allowing for some of the Imbangala to establish the Kingdom of Kasanje
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: After a series of defeats, the Ndongan royal family was driven out of their court in Kabasa, putting the king in exile and allowing for some of the Imbangala to establish the Kingdom of Kasanje.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: The Portuguese governor wanted to proceed with the treaty, but refused to aid Ndongo against the _____ until the king had recaptured Kabasa and been baptized
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Despite her success in the negotiations with the Portuguese, the peace between Ndongo and the Imbangala – themselves engaged in expanding their territory – collapsed. After a series of defeats, the Ndongan royal family was driven out of their court in Kabasa, putting the king in exile and allowing for some of the Imbangala to establish the Kingdom of Kasanje.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: King Mbandi retook Kabasa in _____ and took tentative steps towards Christianity, but remained deeply distrustful of the Portuguese
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: King Mbandi retook Kabasa in 1623 and took tentative steps towards Christianity, but remained deeply distrustful of the Portuguese.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: In addition, the _____ began reneging on the treaty, refusing to withdraw from their fortresses inside Ndongo and conducting raids for loot and slaves into Ndongo's territory
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: The Portuguese governor wanted to proceed with the treaty, but refused to aid Ndongo against the Imbangala until the king had recaptured Kabasa and been baptized. King Mbandi retook Kabasa in 1623 and took tentative steps towards Christianity, but remained deeply distrustful of the Portuguese.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: By _____, King Mbandi had fallen into a deep depression and was forced to cede many of his duties to Nzinga
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: By 1624, King Mbandi had fallen into a deep depression and was forced to cede many of his duties to Nzinga.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: She also assumed the title of _____, conferring a position of great influence among her people
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: She also assumed the title of Ngola, conferring a position of great influence among her people.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: One major obstacle to her rule, her 7-year-old nephew, was under the guardianship of Kasa, an _____ war chief
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: One major obstacle to her rule, her 7-year-old nephew, was under the guardianship of Kasa, an Imbangala war chief.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: According to _____ tradition, neither Nzinga nor her predecessor brother had a direct right to the throne because they were children of slave wives, not the first wife
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: According to Mbande tradition, neither Nzinga nor her predecessor brother had a direct right to the throne because they were children of slave wives, not the first wife.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: While the succession crisis deepened, relations between Ndongo and _____ became more complex
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: While the succession crisis deepened, relations between Ndongo and Portugal became more complex.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Nzinga hoped to fulfill the treaty she had signed with the Portuguese in _____, and thereby regain Ndongan lands lost during her brother's disastrous wars
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Nzinga hoped to fulfill the treaty she had signed with the Portuguese in 1621, and thereby regain Ndongan lands lost during her brother's disastrous wars.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: Governor de _____ was also keen to avoid conflict, and both he and Nzinga were eager to re-open the slave trade that was so vital to the region's economy
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Governor de Sousa was also keen to avoid conflict, and both he and Nzinga were eager to re-open the slave trade that was so vital to the region's economy. However, tensions rose between Nzinga and de Sousa.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: However, tensions rose between Nzinga and de _____
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: Governor de Sousa was also keen to avoid conflict, and both he and Nzinga were eager to re-open the slave trade that was so vital to the region's economy. However, tensions rose between Nzinga and de Sousa.

Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.subject: Ancient India
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.question: De Sousa also demanded that Nzinga become a vassal of the king of _____ and pay tribute, demands she refused outright
Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba.fact: De Sousa also demanded that Nzinga become a vassal of the king of Portugal and pay tribute, demands she refused outright. Pala Empire.subject: Ancient India
Pala Empire.question: He established the _____ monastery and the Somapura Mahavihara
Pala Empire.fact: A few sources written much after Gopala's death mention him as a Buddhist, but it is not known if this is true.  The subsequent Pala kings were definitely Buddhists.  Dharmapala made the Buddhist philosopher Haribhadra his spiritual preceptor.  He established the Vikramashila monastery and the Somapura Mahavihara.  Taranatha also credits him with establishing 50 religious institutions and patronising the Buddhist author Haribhadra.  Devapala restored and enlarged the structures at Somapura Mahavihara, which also features several themes from the epics Ramayana and Mahabharata.  Mahipala I also ordered construction and repairs of several sacred structures at Saranath, Nalanda and Bodh Gaya

Pala Empire.subject: Ancient India
Pala Empire.question: As the rulers of _____'s land, the Palas acquired great reputation in the Buddhist world
Pala Empire.fact: The Palas developed the Buddhist centres of learnings, such as the Vikramashila and the Nalanda universities.  Nalanda, considered one of the first great universities in recorded history, reached its height under the patronage of the Palas.  Noted Buddhist scholars from the Pala period include Atisha, Santaraksita, Saraha, Tilopa, Bimalamitra, Dansheel, Dansree, Jinamitra, Jnanasrimitra, Manjughosh, Muktimitra, Padmanava, Sambhogabajra, Shantarakshit, Silabhadra, Sugatasree and Virachan.  As the rulers of Gautama Buddha's land, the Palas acquired great reputation in the Buddhist world.  Balaputradeva, the Sailendra king of Java, sent an ambassador to him, asking for a grant of five villages for the construction of a monastery at Nalanda.  The request was granted by Devapala.  He appointed the Brahmin Viradeva (of Nagarahara, present-day Jalalabad) as the head of the Nalanda monastery

Pompey.question: On returning to _____, he asked for a triumph to celebrate his victories, an unprecedented demand for someone so young

Pompey.question: When Sulla died in 78 BC, _____ sought to block his state funeral and roll back some of Sulla's laws, then became proconsul of Cisalpine and Transalpine Gaul in January 77 BC

Pompey.subject: Ancient India

Pompey.fact: Principally based in Cilicia, in 68 BC, they raided as far as Ostia, Rome's port, and kidnapped two senators, to general outrage.

Pompey.fact: They were granted lands in cities devastated during the Mithridatic War, notably Soli, renamed Pompeiopolis, and Dyme in Greece, with others sent to towns in Libya and Calabria.

Pompey.fact: In 68 BC, Quintus Marcius Rex replaced Lucullus in Cilicia, while Manius Acilius Glabrio received Bithynia.

Pompey.fact: He also assumed leadership of the war against Mithridates, but failed to respond decisively when the latter reoccupied much of Pontus in 67 BC, then attacked Cappadocia, a Roman ally.
